subject: Spatial analysis with different observations in the same polygon

messages.author: cdab574041a91fc9
messages.subject: Spatial analysis with different observations in the same polygon
parts:
Hi, I'm new into INLA and I don't know how to run a model with different observations in the same polygon. For example, I'm exploring the scotland lip cancer database. In this one, there are counts of 56 counties (56 rows), but I want
to take into account an hypothetical categorical variable e.g. race (black vs white), how could I do that?

What I've tried was the next. I have built two rows for each county, one for each race (112 total rows).

so I have a dataset like this
    cases expected  county.names  AFF  race idareau idareav
1      2    0.350     skye-lochalsh 0.16    white   1          1
2     10    2.175     banff-buchan 0.16    white   2          2
3      3    0.750     caithness       0.10     white   3          3
57      7    1.050     skye-lochalsh 0.16   black   1         1
58     29    6.525  banff-buchan 0.16     black   2          2
59      8    2.250     caithness     0.10     black   3          3

and then, I use a formula like this

res.test2 <- inla(cases~race+AFF+f(idareau,model = "besag", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE)+f(idareav,model="iid"),
+   family = "poisson", data = scotland3,
+   E = expected, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE)
+ )
where,
idareau and idareav are values 1-56 repeated for each race
g is a list of neighbours of the 56 polygons.
The expected values are based on the race population in each county.
County-level variables (e.g. AFF) are repeated in each row of the same county. I mean it is the same value in the rows of white and black of the same county

Is this right? When I try to get the values of each county, fitted.values gives me 112 values, instead of 56. I'd like to have a global estimation of each county

Did I do something wrong? How can I run this type of analysis and get estimates of risk of each county?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial analysis with different observations in the same polygon
parts:
Hi,

Yes, that code looks like it matches the intended model.
You get 112 predictions, since there are 112 combinations of variables (the number of data rows). To see the estimated effect of just the counties, look in $summary.random$idareau, that has just the 56 county-specific latent variables.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial analysis with different observations in the same polygon
parts:
If you want the combined effect of idareau and idareau, you’ll need to either include specific prediction rows in your data.frame (where you set the response variable to NA, and the rest of the row is the combination of covariates you want a prediction for), or use inla.posterior.sample(), from which you can compute arbitrary functionals.

Finn
